title: Local fuel cut on one dividing CIPS condensate: with fuel regrowth stopped only in a disk around it, the body shrinks to 35-45% of its area within ~300 t and lives on as a starved remnant fed by fuel diffusing in across the disk edge, while its fed twin and the 17 bodies outside are unchanged (2/2 seeds)
summary: Asked for by c39's review of 20261026T1025-c40-cips-turnover-divide-claim: a per-individual feed ablation instead of the global fork. world.py is the layered dividing CIPS world (20261026T1100-c40-cips-layered-divide-claim) unchanged; cut.py runs it to t=12000, picks the body whose nearest neighbour is farthest (47-48 px), and branches a fed twin and an arm with kF=0 only inside a disk of radius 0.6x that distance (28-29 px) around it. In the cut arm the mean fuel in the disk drops from 0.77-0.80 to 0.56-0.64 and the target's area (e>0.5) falls from 248 to 96 px (seed 0) and from 221 to 76 px (seed 1) within ~300 t (cut_timecourse.png, cut_s*.png). On seed 1 the remnant stays at ~76 px to t=13500; on seed 0 it regrows to ~160 px. The fed twins keep 248-251 and 221-225 px. The 17 bodies outside the disk are unchanged in both arms; on seed 0 one of them divides at t~13300 (17 -> 18). So each body's size is set by its own fuel supply, but the disk does not starve it to death, because fuel diffuses in from outside (fuel diffusivity DF Lsc^2 = 18).

finding.operator: local feed cut (kF=0 in a disk around one body) in cooperative CIPS on a consumed, regrowing fuel
finding.control: fed twin branched from the same state at t=12000, seeds 0 and 1; bodies outside the disk as internal control
finding.result: target area 248 -> 96 px and 221 -> 76 px within 300 t (fed twins 248-251 and 221-225); remnant persists to t=13500 (seed 0 regrows to 160 px); 17 outside bodies unchanged

limits: A partial result for E: the targeted body shrinks but does not die within 1500 t, so per-body death needs a larger disk (which would also take neighbours' supply) or a lower fuel diffusivity. Two seeds, one disk radius (0.6 x nearest-neighbour distance), one cut time. Body counting outside the disk is approximate (periodic tiling).
